item.title: Reliance group seeks to build satellite capacity for Starlink challenge
item.description: The aim for a low-earth orbit network by 2035 is intended to support the growth of newly-listed unit Jio Platforms ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Mihir Mishra and P R Sanjai Billionaire Mukesh Ambani-led Reliance Group is exploring manufacturing partnerships to support its planned 1,600-satellite broadband constellation, people familiar with the matter said, in a push to create an Indian-controlled alternative to Elon Musk’s Starlink. The aim for a low-earth orbit network by 2035 is intended to support the growth of newly-listed unit Jio Platforms Ltd., the people said, asking not to be identified because the plans are private. Reliance is in talks with Indian satellite manufacturers, technology startups and larger industrial groups on potential partnerships, offering to fund the required infrastructure. The project underscores the challenge facing India’s space ambitions: matching strategic objectives with the manufacturing and launch capacity needed to execute them. India currently produces fewer than 15 satellites a year, according to the people, while the proposed constellation would require output of roughly 200 satellites annually, putting Reliance at the center of efforts to close that gap. The approach mirrors New Delhi’s push to use the private sector to build strategic capabilities, with the Tata Group investing heavily in semiconductor and electronics manufacturing under government-backed initiatives. Reliance plans to combine domestic manufacturing with imports, including at least 400 satellites from the US, as it works toward a September 2027 test mission and a wider deployment beginning in early 2028. The constellation is now targeted for completion by 2035, later than an earlier goal of 2030, due to manufacturing and launch constraints, the people said. The company is in discussions with two US firms regarding potential satellite procurement and is also evaluating suppliers in Europe, they said. It is not considering China as a source for its constellation plans. An email sent to Reliance seeking comments did not elicit any response. The constellation is expected to compete with Starlink in India, but unlike the Musk-backed global network of more than 10,000 satellites, Reliance’s planned system is geared primarily toward meeting India’s connectivity and strategic requirements.Launch FrequencyReliance intends to use the network primarily to improve connectivity across India, though the capability could also serve strategic communication needs during periods of conflict or geopolitical tensions, the people said. Strengthening domestic space capabilities has become key for New Delhi following a recent border conflict with neighbor Pakistan, and is increasing investments in surveillance satellites and partnerships with private space companies.  Industry executives say launch capacity may ultimately prove the bigger challenge. While manufacturing can be expanded with sufficient investment, deploying thousands of satellites will require a significant increase in launch frequency and access to suitable orbital slots. “Manufacturing at scale is doable but the real challenge will be to ensure there are enough rocket launches happening in India for the satellites to be placed in the desired orbit, if the constellation is planned to be implemented with Indian launch vehicles,” said Amal Chandran, CEO of satellite manufacturer HEX20.    Starlink’s entry into India meanwhile remains subject to regulatory and security scrutiny. Concerns over oversight and operational control of foreign satellite networks during periods of geopolitical tension have strengthened the case for domestically controlled alternatives.

Adani Airport launches upgraded rewards membership programme at 8 airports The programme offers discounts on shopping and dining, complimentary lounge access, priority security services, parking facilities and personalised airport assistance, depending on membership category

AAHL Chief Executive Officer Arun Bansal said the response to the earlier programme showed growing passenger interest in airport services beyond air travel | Image: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India Jaipur 1 min read Last Updated : Nov 18 2026 | 1:18 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Adani Airport Holdings Limited (AAHL) has launched an upgraded rewards membership programme at eight airports, including Mumbai, Navi Mumbai and Jaipur airports operated by the company, to offer passengers benefits worth up to ₹65,000 annually. The programme, integrated with the Adani OneApp, offers discounts on shopping and dining, complimentary lounge access, priority security services, parking facilities and personalised airport assistance, depending on the membership category. The benefits will also be available at airports in Ahmedabad, Lucknow, Guwahati, Mangaluru and Thiruvananthapuram, the company said in a statement here. AAHL Chief Executive Officer Arun Bansal said the response to the earlier programme showed growing passenger interest in airport services beyond air travel.   "With Adani Rewards 1.0, we saw 7 million passengers sign up, demonstrating the demand for a more connected relationship with airports," he said. Bansal said the upgraded programme would bring travel, retail, dining and hospitality benefits under a single platform.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

Chinese steel imports remain a threat to Indian industry: Tata Steel CEO India's steel ministry is unlikely to seek fresh curbs on cheap imports in the near term, even as domestic steelmakers pushed for stronger protection

Tata Steel expects to reach an annual production capacity of 40 million metric tons between 2033 and 2035, building on planned capacity expansion through the end of the decade

Reuters 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 18 2026 | 12:04 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Chinese steel imports remain a threat to India's steel industry, Tata Steel CEO T V Narendran said on Wednesday, adding that producers were continuing talks with the government on measures to protect the sector. "We should make sure that Indian industry which is investing significant capital in building capacity, should not be unfairly impacted," Narendran told reporters on the sidelines of an event in New Delhi. India's steel ministry is unlikely to seek fresh curbs on cheap imports in the near term, Reuters reported in October, despite domestic steelmakers' calls for stronger protection. China accounted for nearly a third of India's finished steel imports in the first half of the fiscal year.   Tata Steel expects to reach an annual production capacity of 40 million metric tons between 2033 and 2035, building on planned capacity expansion through the end of the decade. Iron ore costs are rising in India, while Tata Steel continues to source most of its coking coal imports from Australia and smaller volumes from Indonesia, Narendran said. Also Read

The company has no plans to invest in overseas coking coal mines, he added. Separately, Narendran said Tata Steel had sought financial assistance from the Dutch government, with discussions still underway. (Reporting by Neha Arora in New Delhi, writing by Surbhi Misra in Bengaluru; Editing by Nivedita Bhattacharjee and Sherry Jacob-Phillips)

item.title: BlackRock, NBIM, and GIC likely to invest in Bajaj Finance share sale
item.description: Norges Bank Investment Management, GIC and other global funds participated in the ₹11,700 crore institutional placement, alongside major domestic mutual funds ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Rajesh Mascarenhas Norges Bank Investment Management, GIC Pte., BlackRock, FMR LLC, and Capital Group are among global investors that bought shares in Bajaj Finance Ltd.’s 117 billion-rupee ($1.2 billion) institutional offering, according to people familiar with the matter. Nomura Holdings Inc., Goldman Sachs Asset Management and William Blair Investment Management, LLC were also among the investors in the qualified institutional placement, the people said, asking not to be identified because the information is private. ICICI Prudential Asset Management Co. and HDFC Asset Management Co. were among the biggest domestic buyers, the people said. Representatives for the investors didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment. Bajaj Finance approved the allotment of about 114 million shares to eligible qualified institutional buyers at 1,025 rupees apiece, according to a stock exchange filing. The issue price was above the floor price of 992.25 rupees a share. The offering was launched last week at an indicative price that represented a 4.99% discount to the previous close. Proceeds will be used to repay deposits, loans, commercial paper and non-convertible debentures, as well as for interest payments and other purposes, according to the deal terms. The share sale followed Bajaj Finance’s Nov. 10 allotment of 57.43 million warrants to promoter and holding company Bajaj Finserv Ltd. at 1,010 rupees apiece, raising about 58 billion rupees, according to an exchange filing. Large Indian equity offerings have picked up after Jio Platforms Ltd.’s record $3.1 billion IPO last month and a rebound in the secondary market in November. The recovery has helped revive investor appetite for big-ticket transactions after a relatively weak first half of the year. Kotak Mahindra Capital Co., Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan Chase & Co., IIFL Capital Services Ltd., Axis Capital Ltd. and JM Financial Ltd. worked on the transaction.
